questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Pivot Columns of a Matrix
questions.problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $A$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $A$ has $2$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns.

questions.problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $A$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $A$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $4$th columns.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Non-Pivot Columns of a Matrix in Row Echelon Form
questions.problem:
The row echelon form matrix $A$ is given below. What are its **non**-pivot columns?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $A$ has $3$ pivots in the $1$st, $2$nd and $4$th columns:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the only non-pivot columns are the $3$rd and $5$th columns.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Number of Pivot Columns of a Matrix
questions.problem:
Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $B,$ given by

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 & -5 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 & -6 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $B$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 & -5 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 & -6 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -8 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $B$ has $4$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $4.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Number of Pivot Columns of a Matrix
questions.problem:
Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $D,$ given by

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 7 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $D$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 7 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 7 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -4 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $D$ has $3$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $3.$
